title: Rooted — Spring 2026
coverLines: A seed is not in a hurry
Thirteen weeks to a strong tree
summary: Spring 2026 study guide for Sprout Kids (6–8): thirteen weeks of growing — from a tiny seed to a tree with deep roots. One verse, one try-it and one prayer for every day of the season.

blocks.text: How to use this study guide

This is a study guide for Sprout Kids families. Spring has thirteen weeks, so we grow one thing a week — from a tiny seed to a tree with deep roots. Each day has a verse to read out loud, two or three lines to think about, a short Try it list, and a prayer to say together. Read together at one meal or one quiet corner, put the verse card somewhere you'll see it, and watch a small seed grow a strong tree.
Spring grows

In Spring the ground wakes up. A seed you planted in the dark, damp soil becomes a green shoot, then a stem, then a tree that gives shade and fruit. Real trees grow slowly — day by day, bit by bit. God is growing you the same way: one verse, one kind word, one brave try at a time.

Follow the steps on each day: read the verse, read the lines, do the Try it, then say the prayer. On day 5 of each week there's a little quiz to see what you remember. On day 7 you get to rest and think — draw, write or talk it over. At the end of the season you will have a tree you grew yourself.

intro.text: This week we plant the smallest seed of all — a beginning the size of a dot — and we watch what God can grow from something that small. Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is exactly like that.

verse.text: The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man took and planted in his field.

blocks.text: A mustard seed is hardly bigger than a grain of sand. You could lose it between your fingers. Yet when it grows, it becomes a tree big enough for birds to nest in. God loves starting big things from tiny seeds — and you are one of His seeds today.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find the tiniest seed or pebble you can and hold it in your hand
Say today's verse together out loud, twice
Put a small sticker on today's date to mark the first seed of your spring

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for starting something new today
Ask Him to grow you, a little bit, this spring

verse.text: Night and day, whether he sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.

blocks.text: The farmer cannot see the seed grow. He sleeps, he wakes, he does his chores — and under the soil the seed is quietly doing its work. Growing does not need you to watch it. It needs you to stay planted in good soil and keep trusting the Gardener.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Draw a seed under the ground, with tiny roots going down
Do one small good thing without telling anyone
Say: 'God is growing me, even when I can't see it'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell God one thing you are waiting for Him to grow
Ask for patience like the farmer

verse.text: Unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds.

blocks.text: One seed, buried and forgotten, becomes many seeds. That is how God thinks: a little bit given away turns into much more. When you share a crayon, a pencil or a snack, your one small seed is becoming many seeds in someone else's day.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Share one thing with someone and watch what grows
Plant a seed of thanks in a sentence to a grown-up
Count how many people your one act of kindness touched

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give God one thing you want to share this spring
Thank Him that He does not stay small — He multiplies

verse.text: Who dares despise the day of small things?

blocks.text: Everyone loves the giant tree and the giant story. But every tree begins as a dot nobody noticed. Do not look down on small beginnings — the first page of a book, the first wobbly steps, the first shy prayer. God counts them all.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start one 'small thing' — read one line of a book, one star in the sky
Do it again tomorrow, and the next day
Tell someone: 'small things matter to God'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for your ordinary small day
Ask Him to make it grow into something good

verse.text: The seed sprouts and grows — first the stalk, then the head, then the full kernel in the head.

blocks.text: Growing has an order: first the little green stalk, then the head, then the full grain. Nothing good grows all at once. Today's quiz is about where good seeds grow and what order they grow in.

blocks.question: Which one grows a kernel of wheat: a bad seed in a cold corner, or a good seed that stays planted and waits?
options: The bad seed in the cold corner
The good seed that stays planted and waits
blocks.explain: Right — the seed that stays planted and waits is the one God grows. Patience is part of growing!

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a patient heart today
Thank Him that He knows the order of your growing

verse.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

blocks.text: Even the busy seed rests in the dark soil. Sunday is God's gift of a rest day — a day to be still, not to hurry, and to remember that He is God and we are His. Quiet days are part of growing strong.

blocks.prompt: Be still for one whole minute. What do you notice? Write it down or tell someone.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest quietly with God today
Thank Him that He is in charge of your growing

verse.text: I will pour water on the thirsty land, and streams on the dry ground.

blocks.text: Your seed has spent its first week in the soil. Now God the Gardener is pouring water — and He says He will also pour out His Spirit on you, like water on thirsty ground. Draw what your seed might look like on day 7.

blocks.prompt: Draw your seed at the end of week 1 — what does it look like under the soil?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to 'water' your heart this week
Thank Him for the whole first week of Spring

intro.text: This week we give our seed its water — God's words. A seed does not choose its own drink; it drinks what the Gardener gives. You grow the same way: you drink in God's Word, and your roots reach down into it.

verse.text: His delight is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he meditates day and night.

blocks.text: The word 'meditate' just means chewing on something slowly, like a cow chews grass. You meditate on God's words when you read one, say it out loud, and think about it while you walk to school. Water goes down slowly too — but it is what makes everything grow.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say today's verse three times — slow and loud
Drink a glass of water and think: this is like God's Word for my heart
Put your verse card where you brush your teeth

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make His Word tasty to you
Thank Him that His words are water for you

verse.text: They will be like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither.

blocks.text: A tree that sits by a stream never has to be scared of a dry day — its roots are already drinking. A child who reads God's Word has that same calm. Dry days will come, but your roots know where the water is.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find a tree near your home and look at its roots if you can
Read one verse from a Bible, not just an app, with a grown-up
Say: 'I am planted by the stream'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the gift of His Word
Ask Him to keep your roots by the stream

verse.text: Rooted and built up in him, strengthened in the faith.

blocks.text: The part of the tree you cannot see matters most. Without roots, nothing else stands. The part of your life nobody claps for — your quiet prayers, your Bible time, obeying at home — is the roots. Keep growing them.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do one 'root thing' nobody will see today
Tell a grown-up one thing you learned from the Bible this week
Trace a root pattern in the air with your finger

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to grow your roots deep and quiet
Thank Him for the hidden parts of your growing

verse.text: Faith comes from hearing the message, and the message is heard through the word about Christ.

blocks.text: How does faith come? It comes by hearing. Somebody reads God's Word, and you hear it, and that hearing is water for your heart. That is why reading out loud together matters so much — your ears water your roots.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Read a Bible verse to a grown-up or a sibling, out loud
Listen to someone read a verse to you
Say where your 'water' comes from today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the people who read His Word to you
Ask Him to keep you listening

verse.text: My soul thirsts for God, for the living God.

blocks.text: You can give a plant any water — but only clean water makes it grow well. Today's little quiz is about which water works.

blocks.question: What drink does a soul need to grow strong in God?
options: Screens and complaining — the junk drink
blocks.explain: Yes! Our souls thirst for God, and His Word is the drink that satisfies.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell God: 'my soul is thirsty for You'
Ask Him to fill you with His Word today

verse.text: Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road.

blocks.text: God wants His words to travel with families — at breakfast, on the walk, in the car. Water is easier to drink when the whole family drinks together. Rest day: choose the family verse you will say all season.

blocks.prompt: Pick a verse for your whole family to say this spring. Write it or tell them.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray for your family to drink God's Word together
Thank God for the family you grow in

verse.text: How sweet are your words to my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth!

blocks.text: God's words are not boring medicine — they are sweet as honey. Today, fill your week-jar with one verse you love, and repeat it like a song while you play.

blocks.prompt: Write your favourite verse of the week and the word that tastes sweetest to you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make His words sweet in your mouth
Thank Him for two full weeks of Spring

intro.text: A plant needs water — and it also needs sun. Prayer is the sunlight for your soul. This week we turn our faces toward God, again and again, like leaves turning toward the light.

verse.text: Pray continually.

blocks.text: The shortest verse-power in the Bible. 'Pray continually' does not mean glue your eyes shut. It means your heart can turn to God all day — while you swing, while you walk, a little hello and a thank-you all through the day.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Send God three tiny 'hello's' during your day
Fold your hands at lunch and say thanks out loud
Count how many times you remembered to pray

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help you remember Him all day
Thank Him for listening every time

verse.text: When you pray, go into your room, close the door and pray to your Father.

blocks.text: Jesus says prayer is not a show for other people. You close the door, and you talk to your Father who loves you. Your quiet corner, your bedside, the secret place — that is where the sun shines brightest.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask a grown-up to help you make a 'prayer corner' — cushion, candle or no candle, just a spot
Say a private prayer there, door closed
Don't tell anyone you did it — prayer is between you and God

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that your prayers do not need to be a performance
Tell Him something only you and He know

verse.text: Three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed and gave thanks before his God.

blocks.text: Daniel did not stop praying to stay safe — he prayed BECAUSE he trusted God. Morning, noon and night, his knees bent and his heart turned toward God, even when it was hard. His habit had already decided for him.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pray once in the morning, once at noon, once at night
Each time, thank God for one thing and ask for one thing
Say: 'my knees bend for God'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for faithful people like Daniel
Ask God for a habit of prayer like Daniel's

verse.text: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.

blocks.text: Praying is asking, seeking, knocking — and the answer is always that God is good. Sometimes He gives what you asked. Sometimes He gives something better. But He never slams the door; the door opens.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask God for something small and specific today
Look for His answer — it may come through a person
Write your ask down so you can thank Him later

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask boldly — God is able
Thank Him for the door that opens

verse.text: Jesus told his disciples a parable to show them that they should always pray and not give up.

blocks.text: The sun does not shine once and stop; it shines every day. Prayer is like that — 'always pray and not give up'. Little quiz time for our sunny week!

blocks.question: Jesus told us to pray and... what?
blocks.explain: Yes! 'Always pray and not give up.' The sun never stops shining, and we never stop praying.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for never-give-up prayer
Thank Him for the sunshine of your week

verse.text: The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.

blocks.text: This is the most beautiful blessing in the Bible. 'Make his face shine on you' — that is God smiling at you, like the sun warming a leaf. Rest day: let someone bless you, and bless someone back.

blocks.prompt: Who can you bless today? Say the Numbers blessing over them (or write the words).

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive God's smile over you today
Bless another person with your words

verse.text: The Lord God is a sun and shield; the Lord bestows favour and honour.

blocks.text: God is not just like sunlight — He is a sun and shield. He warms you AND protects you. Make your sunlight list of people and things to pray for, one per finger, and pray your hand every day.

blocks.prompt: Write or draw five people to pray for — one for each finger of your hand.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray your five fingers of prayer
Thank God for three weeks of Spring growing

intro.text: A seed can have all the water and sun in the world — but if the soil is hard or full of weeds, it cannot grow. This week we get our hearts ready: soft, good soil for God's seeds.

verse.text: But the seed on good soil stands for those with a noble and good heart, who hear the word, retain it, and by persevering produce a crop.

blocks.text: Jesus told a story about a farmer scattering seed. Some fell on the path (the birds ate it), some on rocks (it dried up), some among thorns (it was choked), and some on good soil — and THAT one produced a crop. A good heart is soft, open soil.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find the softest patch of soil or sand you can and press your finger in
Say: 'Lord, make my heart good soil'
When you hear God's Word today, keep it in your heart — don't let birds take it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your heart soft good soil
Thank Him that He is the farmer who plants in you

verse.text: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you.

blocks.text: We do not have to fix our own hearts and then come to God. He gives us the new heart. Like a gardener turning over hard soil, God is gentle and able to change the ground He planted in.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let a grown-up help you 'turn over' something hard in your heart with a prayer
Ask God for one new, softer thing inside you
Treat your heart like a garden you keep clean

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to give you a new heart
Thank Him that He changes us gently

verse.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

blocks.text: Good soil is gentle soil. When an angry word flies at you, you get to choose your answer. A soft, gentle answer is like water on a fire; a harsh word is like throwing oil.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Practise your 'gentle answer' voice today — soft and slow
Try 'can we try again?' instead of the sharp word
Notice what happens when you answer gently

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to give you a gentle answer today
Thank Him for gentle people in your life

verse.text: Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other, just as in Christ God forgave you.

blocks.text: Forgiveness is what keeps garden soil soft. If we hold grudges, the soil packs hard and nothing grows. God forgave you in Christ — so you can pass that same forgiveness along today.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Forgive someone today — out loud, even if they do not hear
Ask for forgiveness from someone you hurt
Say: 'I forgive you, just like God forgave me'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for forgiving you completely
Give Him your grudges to pull out like weeds

verse.text: Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

blocks.text: Time for our good-soil quiz! Remember the farmer's field — there were four kinds of ground.

blocks.question: Which ground made the seed grow into a whole crop?
blocks.explain: Yes! Only the good soil — a noble, good heart that keeps God's word — produces the crop.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to keep your heart soft
Thank Him for the seed He is growing in you

verse.text: The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing.

blocks.text: Good soil can rest. It does not have to do everything at once. The Shepherd gently leads, and in green pastures even the soil of our hearts can lie down and be quiet.

blocks.prompt: What does a restful Sunday look like for you? Draw or describe your green pasture.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest in the Shepherd's care today
Thank Him for the good soil of your week

verse.text: Create in me a pure heart, O God.

blocks.text: David, who made big mistakes, prayed this: 'Create in me a pure heart.' Our hearts are not perfect — but they can be soft before God every day, ready for Him to make them new.

blocks.prompt: What is one way you will keep your heart soft this week? Write your plan.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray David's prayer: 'create in me a pure heart'
Thank God for four weeks of Spring growing

intro.text: Weeds steal water, sun and space from good plants. In our hearts, the weeds are the little sins — anger, worry, unkind words. This week we learn to spot them and pull them out by the root.

verse.text: Human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.

blocks.text: Anger is a weed. It grows fast and takes over, and it never grows anything God wants. That does not mean you never feel angry — it means you do not let the weed own your garden.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one 'weed' feeling in your garden today (anger? worry? sharp words?)
When it shows up, take three slow breaths
Talk to a grown-up about it instead of letting it grow

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give God the weed of anger today
Ask Him to plant patience where the weed was

verse.text: The words of the reckless pierce like swords, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.

blocks.text: Some of the worst weeds grow from words. A sharp word pierces like a sword. A wise, kind word heals. You cannot pull a weed you will not name — so name the words that hurt, and choose the ones that heal.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Notice one sharp word today and turn it into a healing one
Practise a healing sentence: 'I'm sorry' is a good one
Tell someone how their kind words helped you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help your tongue bring healing
Thank Him for people whose words built you up

verse.text: Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.

blocks.text: Weeds hate two things: listening and waiting. When you are quick to listen and slow to speak, the anger weed runs out of food. Slow things—like listening—are actually the fast way to peace.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Play at being 'slow to speak': count to three before you say anything big
Be quick to listen to someone all the way to the end
Tell a grown-up: 'I'm practising slow anger'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for quick ears and a slow tongue
Thank Him that peace grows where patience is

verse.text: Do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself.

blocks.text: Worry is a sneaky weed — it looks like nothing, then suddenly it is everywhere. Jesus says today has enough of its own; tomorrow is not yours to carry yet. You carry today, and you carry it with God.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one worry and give it to God like a weed in your hands
Do not talk about tomorrow's test — just do today well
Say: 'tomorrow is God's, today is mine to live'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand God your worry-weed today
Ask Him for strength for today only

verse.text: Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire. Thus, by their fruit you will recognise them.

blocks.text: You can tell a weed from a good plant by its fruit. Time for our weed quiz!

blocks.question: Which of these is a HEART-WEED that steals food from the good plant?
options: A grumpy, harsh word that pokes
blocks.explain: Yes! Harsh words are weeds. Pull them out, and plant a soft answer instead.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Show God one weed to pull this week
Ask Him to help you recognise weeds by their fruit

verse.text: The peace of God, which transcends all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds.

blocks.text: Rest day, and the weeds have been busy all week — but God has a guard for your heart and mind: His peace. A weeded garden is quiet, clear, and calm. Let that peace stand guard over you.

blocks.prompt: What does 'peace on the inside' feel like to you? Draw or write a picture of it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God's peace to guard your heart and mind
Thank Him for the rest of a weeded week

verse.text: Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

blocks.text: Half of pulling weeds is knowing what they look like. Today we make a list — the things we know crowd out God's good growth — so next week, when they show up, we recognize them and pull fast.

blocks.prompt: List the weeds YOU have to watch for (anger, worry, harsh words, selfishness...). Pick one to pull this week.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give God your weed list
Thank Him for five full weeks of Spring growing

intro.text: The soil is ready, the weeds are pulled — now watch the green! This week we meet the sprout that pushes up through hard ground. That is courage: growing even when it is a little scary.

verse.text: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged, for the Lord your God will be with you wherever you go.

blocks.text: This was God's pep-talk to Joshua when everything felt huge and new. Courage is not about feeling big — it is about remembering that God is WITH you. That is how a tiny sprout breaks hard ground.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do one brave, small thing today (say hello, try the scary slide, raise your hand)
Say Joshua 1:9 out loud before you do it
Tell someone you were brave BECAUSE God is with you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for courage for one thing today
Thank Him that He is with you wherever you go

verse.text: This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it.

blocks.text: A sprout does not wait for tomorrow to be born. Today, right now, is the day God made — and He made it for rejoicing. Courage often starts with a 'yes' to today.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say 'this is the day' the moment you wake up
Enjoy one ordinary wonderful thing today
Smile at someone — joy is courageous

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the exact day He made
Ask Him to fill it with gladness

verse.text: Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you and help you.

blocks.text: The sprout never sees the roots holding it — but they are there. God says 'I WILL strengthen you'; it is His promise, not yours to earn. When your legs are wobbly, His Hand is the root.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find the verse 'Do not fear, for I am with you' in a Bible with a grown-up
Act it out: stand on one leg and say it twice — you are held
Every time you wobble today, say the verse

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to strengthen you and help you
Thank Him that He is your God

verse.text: For God has not given us a spirit of fear, but of power, of love and of a sound mind.

blocks.text: Fear is a feel, but it is not our gift from God. He gives power, love and a clever, calm mind. That is the sprout's secret: it moves with God's power, not its own.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Catch fear today and say: 'that is not my gift'
Breathe in 'power, love, calm mind'
Use God's sound mind: think before you act

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a calm mind today
Thank Him that fear is not from Him

verse.text: Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous.

blocks.text: A sprout's quiz to finish the week — one point for each brave 'yes' you remember!

blocks.question: Why can you be brave?
options: Because God is with me — He commanded me to be strong
Because I am the biggest sprout in the garden
blocks.explain: Yes! We are brave because GOD is with us — not because we are big.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that courage comes from Him
Ask Him to help you obey the command to be strong

verse.text: The Lord is my light and my salvation — whom shall I fear?

blocks.text: Rest day — and this is a bold song! Light and salvation belong to God, so the question 'whom shall I fear?' answers itself. We rest tonight in a God who is light and safety.

blocks.prompt: Draw a picture of a place where you feel safe and light. Thank God for being your light.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for being your light
Let the fear questions go and rest in Him

verse.text: I can do all this through him who gives me strength.

blocks.text: The sprout grew leaves this week. Think back — what did YOU try that took brave? Write it down so you remember: you can do hard things through Christ who gives you strength.

blocks.prompt: Write about one brave thing you did this week, and thank God for the strength.
blocks.placeholder: This week I was brave when I...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for every brave 'yes' this week
Ask for strength for next week's growing

intro.text: The sprout becomes a stem — and a stem grows straight toward the light. This week is about truth: growing straight means telling the truth, even when bending feels easier.

verse.text: The integrity of the upright guides them.

blocks.text: Integrity is a grown-up word for being the same on the outside as you are on the inside. A stem that bends hides nothing. Your honesty is a guide — it steers you down the straight path.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Practise 'the same on the inside and outside' with one small thing
Tell the truth the first time — quick and straight
Straighten your own shoulders like a straight stem

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help you grow straight
Thank Him that His path is not crooked

verse.text: Therefore each of you must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to your neighbour.

blocks.text: A lie is like a shadow the stem casts to look taller. God says: take off the shadow, speak truthfully. Truth is lighter to carry and you grow in the open.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: No shadow-words today — no 'un-truths', even small ones
If you bend, come back straight: 'I want to say that again, truthfully'
Thank someone for being truthful with you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help your words be true
Thank Him for speaking truth to us

verse.text: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much.

blocks.text: Grown-ups learn to trust you one small thing at a time. Tell the truth about the tiny things — the juice spill, the missing sock — and you become the child they can trust with big things later.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be trustworthy with one tiny task (water the plant, feed the pet)
If something goes wrong, tell the truth before you are asked
Say to a grown-up: 'you can trust me with the little things'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be a child God can trust
Thank Him for entrusting you with a garden

verse.text: The Lord detests lying lips, but he delights in people who are trustworthy.

blocks.text: Did you know God has favourites of joy? He delights — He rejoices — in truthful children. Not in perfect children; in honest ones. A straight answer is a heart offering.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one straight answer even when it is the hard one
Watch how a truthful answer makes a grown-up smile
Say: 'God delights in trustworthy people — I can be one'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He delights in your honest heart
Ask Him to help you be trustworthy

verse.text: The Lord is faithful, and he will strengthen you and protect you from the evil one.

blocks.text: Stem made a quiz for us! Pick the straight answer.

blocks.question: What does God delight in?
blocks.explain: Right! God delights in trustworthy people — the ones who grow straight.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is faithful
Ask Him to strengthen you to be trustworthy

verse.text: Lord, who may dwell in your sacred tent? ... The one whose walk is blameless, who does what is righteous, and speaks the truth from their heart.

blocks.text: Rest day: the psalm asks who is invited to 'dwell in God's tent' — the answer is people who speak truth from their heart. You do not dwell there because you are perfect; you dwell there because God is good, and He loves a true heart.

blocks.prompt: What does a 'truthful heart' look like at rest? Draw or write your picture of it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest in God's tent today
Thank Him that He welcomes true hearts

verse.text: Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will grow to become in every respect the mature body of him who is the head, that is, Christ.

blocks.text: Truth has one more secret: it must be said IN LOVE. Truth without love is a stick; truth with love is a stem. Write your sentence for the week — a true thing, said kindly.

blocks.prompt: Write a TRUE thing you need to say to someone this week — said in a kind way.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help you speak truth in love
Thank Him for seven weeks of straight growing

intro.text: The stem is straight and now the leaves reach out. Leaves are the helping hands of the tree — they catch the light and pass it on. This week is about hands that serve, like Jesus' hands.

verse.text: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

blocks.text: Doing good can be tiring, and sometimes it seems nobody noticed. But leaves keep working all season. God says your good help is not wasted — the harvest comes at the proper time.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do one act of help nobody will clap for
When you get tired of helping, keep going one more time
Say: 'my harvest is coming'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for strength to keep helping
Thank Him that your good work is not wasted

verse.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.

blocks.text: If Jesus — the King — came to serve and not to be served, then serving is not a small job. It is a royal job. Every time your hands help, you are doing what Jesus did.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Serve someone before they even ask (pass, fetch, carry)
Serve without announcing it
Say: 'like Jesus, I serve today'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for serving you first
Ask Him to make your hands like His

verse.text: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters.

blocks.text: What if the person you are REALLY working for is the Lord? Then the boring job — tidying, homework, dishes — becomes worship. Leaves do their small work with all their heart.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pick one chore and do it 'for the Lord' — as well as you can
Notice the difference it makes in your heart
Tell a grown-up you worked as for the Lord

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Offer your day's work to the Lord
Thank Him for work that matters to Him

verse.text: Now that I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another's feet.

blocks.text: On the night before He died, Jesus knelt and washed His friends' dusty feet. The King doing the servant's job — and saying 'do this too'. Serving the lowliest way is following Jesus closest.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find the lowest 'foot-washing' job at home and take it
Help a younger child the same way you would want help
Say: 'Jesus washed feet, so I can serve small'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for kneeling to serve
Ask for a servant's heart like His

verse.text: Very truly I tell you, whoever believes in me will do the works I have been doing.

blocks.text: Leaves say it is quiz time — reach for the right answer!

blocks.question: Jesus said He came to be served or to serve?
blocks.explain: Yes! 'The Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve.' We follow Him by serving.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for a week of serving hands
Ask Him to show you who to help next

verse.text: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.

blocks.text: Rest day: even helpers need helping. God is not a distant helper — He is 'ever-present', right here, in every trouble. Rest under His shade.

blocks.prompt: Who helped you this week? Write them and thank God for every one.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for being ever-present
Thank Him for people who have been His hands to you

verse.text: Then the King will say, 'Whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.'

blocks.text: Here is a beautiful surprise: when you help the smallest, least important person, Jesus says it is like helping HIM. Trace your hands, and remember: those hands served Jesus this week.

blocks.prompt: Trace both your hands. Inside each one, write or draw someone you helped this week.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Offer your hands to Jesus
Thank Him for the week of reaching leaves

intro.text: The leaves are out, and now — a bud. A bud is a promise curled up tight, waiting for its time. This week we learn patience: the bloom comes at just the right moment, not before.

verse.text: See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

blocks.text: Even the farmer cannot rush a crop. He waits for the rains; then he waits for the seed; then he waits for the harvest. Waiting is not wasted time — it is the working time. The bud is growing inside.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Watch something grow that you cannot rush (a plant, a sunflower)
When you want to rush, say: 'the farmer waits'
Name one thing worth waiting for

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a waiting heart
Thank Him for the rains He sends in your life

verse.text: But those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles.

blocks.text: Hope in the Lord is the secret of the bud. Waiting on God is not sitting still out of boredom — it is waiting with your eyes up. When you hope in the Lord, strength comes back like new.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wait with your eyes up, not down: hope in the Lord
When you feel tired, say: 'my strength is renewing'
Do the eagle thing: spread your arms and breathe slow

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Put your hope in the Lord today
Ask Him to renew your strength

verse.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

blocks.text: God is the maker of seasons. He made seed-time and harvest-time, and He made your growing in nice, patient order. You are not late and you are not early — you are exactly in season.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Notice the season outside your window today
Tell God: 'I trust Your timing'
Don't compare your tree to your friend's tree

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He made seasons and timing
Ask Him to help you be content in your season

verse.text: I wait for the Lord, my whole being waits, and in his word I put my hope.

blocks.text: What do you do while the bud waits? The psalm says: wait for the Lord, and put your hope in His word. Waiting with God's word in your heart is never an empty waiting.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Fill one waiting moment with a Bible verse instead of a screen
When you wait in a line, pray a short prayer
Say: 'my waiting belongs to God'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Offer God your waiting moments
Thank Him for His word to hope in

verse.text: The Lord is good to those whose hope is in him, to the one who seeks him.

blocks.text: Bud quiz! Choose what patience really is.

blocks.question: Patience is...
options: Trusting God's timing while you keep growing
blocks.explain: Yes! Patience is trusting God's timing AND keeping your roots drinking all the while.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is good to those who hope
Ask Him to make you patient in your growing

verse.text: Be still before the Lord and wait patiently for him.

blocks.text: Rest day — the bud is safe in its shell; nothing is rushing it. Being still before the Lord is a rest-day skill. The bud does not fight to bloom; it rests and trusts.

blocks.prompt: Describe or draw a bud curling up safely before it opens. What is your 'safe waiting' place?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Be still before the Lord today
Thank Him for rest in the middle of waiting

verse.text: For I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.

blocks.text: God saw all of this coming. He knows the plan — and it is a good one. Write your bud diary: the thing you are waiting for, and the promise you are standing on.

blocks.prompt: Write one thing you are waiting for and the verse you will wait on.
blocks.placeholder: I am waiting for... and I will wait on...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for His good plans for you
Ask Him for hope for the future

intro.text: It happened — the bud cracked open into blossoms! Blossoms are joy made visible. This week we open up too: we sing, we thank, we rejoice. Joy IS the bloom of a soul well-watered.

verse.text: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!

blocks.text: Paul wrote 'rejoice' twice, as if we needed to hear the joke twice to really get it. Joy is not the same as happiness; happiness depends on what happens, joy depends on the Lord. And the Lord is always faithful.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find three reasons to rejoice in the Lord today
Say, 'I will say it again: rejoice!' when things go sour
Make a joyful noise somewhere quiet today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that joy comes from Him, not from happenings
Ask Him for a rejoicing heart today

verse.text: Shout for joy to the Lord, all the earth. Worship the Lord with gladness; come before him with joyful songs.

blocks.text: Blossoms do not whisper; they shout with colour. The psalm invites you to welcome God with gladness — with songs, with your loudest happy sounds. God loves a child who is glad to see Him.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Sing one happy song — loud, even a little silly
Come to prayer with gladness today
Make up a 'joyful noise' verse about God

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Worship God with gladness today
Thank Him for songs and flowers and joyful noise

verse.text: Give thanks in all circumstances; for this is God's will for you in Christ Jesus.

blocks.text: Thanks is the blossom's perfume! 'Give thanks in all circumstances' is not pretending bad things are good — it is trusting God is with us in them, and so there is always something to thank Him for.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start and end the day with one 'thank you'
Thank God in a hard moment, not just the happy ones
Give someone a thank-you bloom today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God in all your circumstances today
Ask Him to grow thanks out of everything

verse.text: In the morning, Lord, you hear my voice; in the morning I lay my requests before you and wait expectantly.

blocks.text: Blossoms open first thing in the morning. The psalm lets God be the first to hear our voice each day — our requests laid out like petals, offered before the day begins. Expectantly: we know He answers.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Before breakfast, say one thing to God first
Lay your request 'before Him' — out loud
And then smile: you are heard

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give God your morning, first thing
Ask Him to meet you expectantly

verse.text: The joy of the Lord is your strength.

blocks.text: A blossom quiz to open your week!

blocks.question: Where does our strength come from when we rejoice?
blocks.explain: Yes! 'The joy of the Lord is your strength.' Rejoicing makes you strong.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for joy that makes you strong
Ask Him to fill you with His joy

verse.text: I will extol the Lord at all times; his praise will always be on my lips.

blocks.text: Rest day among the blossoms. 'At all times' is a big promise — and it is a GIFT: praise keeps our hearts facing God's beauty no matter what happened this week.

blocks.prompt: What is the most beautiful blossom of your week? Write a tiny praise for it.
blocks.placeholder: This week I praise God for...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Praise God at rest today
Thank Him for the blossoms of your week

verse.text: And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus.

blocks.text: Today we pick a whole bouquet! List your joys like flowers you have grown through this spring, and give God the whole bunch. He loves receiving what He grew.

blocks.prompt: Make your blossom bouquet: list five joys from this spring.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Offer God your bouquet of joys
Thank Him for ten weeks of Spring growing

intro.text: Blossoms become fruit — fruit the whole garden can taste. This week is about the 'fruit of the Spirit': love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Fruit you can share.

verse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness.

blocks.text: Try to say that list in one breath: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness — plus gentleness and self-control (verse 23). This is what the Spirit grows INSIDE you, like fruit on a tree.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Learn the first five fruits off by heart
Choose ONE fruit of the Spirit to grow today — point to it
Let someone 'taste' it when you show it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Spirit to grow His fruit in you
Thank God for the fruit of His Spirit

verse.text: A new command I give you: love one another. As I have loved you, so you must love one another.

blocks.text: Love is the first and biggest fruit. Jesus loves us a certain way — patiently, kindly, all the way — and He says: love each other THAT way. That is a new, beautiful, do-able love.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Love someone the way Jesus loves you — patiently and kindly
Do one loving thing before being asked
Ask 'how can I love you today?' to someone close

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for how He loves you
Ask Him to teach your heart to love like that

verse.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.

blocks.text: Here is the biggest secret of the whole garden: fruit does not come from effort alone — it comes from staying CONNECTED to Jesus, the vine. Remain in Him, and fruit grows almost by itself.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stay 'connected' today: pray, read, talk to Jesus
Notice fruit you did not even try to grow
Say: 'I am a branch — Jesus is my vine'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to remain in the vine today
Thank Jesus that connected branches bear fruit

verse.text: Clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.

blocks.text: You dress yourself in the morning. God says: also 'clothe yourselves' in kindness and gentleness — put them on like your favourite coat. Fruit is worn, not just grown.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Put on 'kindness' for the whole day — treat it like a coat
Add patience and gentleness to the outfit
At night, 'take off' the tired clothes with a thank you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to clothe you in His character today
Thank Him for kindness you have seen

verse.text: ...gentleness and self-control.

blocks.text: Time to taste the quiz! Which fruit is ripe in your hand today?

blocks.question: The FIRST fruit of the Spirit is...?
blocks.explain: Yes! 'The fruit of the Spirit is love...' — love comes first and feeds every other fruit.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for the first, biggest fruit: love
Thank Him for gentleness and self-control too

verse.text: Taste and see that the Lord is good.

blocks.text: Rest day, and the fruit is ready! 'Taste and see' — God is not a distant idea. He is good that you can actually experience, like a sweet fruit on your tongue. Rest today and taste His goodness.

blocks.prompt: When have you 'tasted' that God is good? Write or draw one memory.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Taste and see the Lord's goodness
Thank Him for the fruit of this season

verse.text: They will still bear fruit in old age; they will stay fresh and green.

blocks.text: Trees that stay near God keep bearing fruit their whole lives — they stay 'fresh and green'. Draw your tree today with the fruits the Spirit has been growing in you.

blocks.prompt: Draw your tree and write on the fruit the Spirit is growing in you (love, joy, peace...).

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the fruit He is growing in you
Ask Him to keep you fresh and green all your life

intro.text: Every garden gets a storm. This week is about the tree with deep roots at the end of the Psalms and the house built on rock in Matthew — because hard days WILL come, and the deep-rooted tree is the one that stands.

verse.text: The rain came down, the streams rose, and the winds blew and beat against that house; yet it did not fall, because it had its foundation on the rock.

blocks.text: Jesus told a story of two builders. One built on sand; the storm knocked it flat. One built on rock; the same storm could not move it. The difference was not the storm — it was the foundation. Ours is Jesus.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Talk about your 'rock': Jesus — the firm place under you
When a mini-storm comes today (loud voices, unfair things), stand on the Rock
Say: 'my foundation is Jesus'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus that He is your rock
Ask Him to hold you when storms come

verse.text: They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves are always green.

blocks.text: Jeremiah draws a tree whose roots reach the stream — so when the hot, dry season comes, it does not fear. Hard days do not make a rooted child panic; the roots know where to drink.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: When 'heat' comes today, drink from the Word
Observe a tree in the sun and notice its calm
Say: 'I have roots, I do not fear the heat'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for streams in dry places
Ask Him to keep your leaves green in any weather

verse.text: The Lord himself goes before you and will be with you; he will never leave you nor forsake you. Do not be afraid; do not be discouraged.

blocks.text: Storm days can feel so alone. But God promises He will never leave you and never forsake you — double 'never's. He goes BEFORE you, so even the scariest path already has His footprints on it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Whisper 'never leave me, never forsake me' when you feel alone
Look for one 'footprint' of God ahead of you today
Be brave: He goes before you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God He never leaves you
Ask Him to go before you today

verse.text: He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, 'Quiet! Be still!' Then the wind died down and it was completely calm.

blocks.text: Jesus was asleep in a boat, and a big storm came, and His friends panicked. But the One who was sleeping is the One who made the wind. He said two words — 'Quiet! Be still!' — and the storm obeyed. He can say those words to your storms too.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: When your heart is stormy, say 'Quiet! Be still!' and call on Jesus
Remember: Jesus is in your boat
Practise a calm, still heart before bed

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to quiet the storms in your heart
Thank Him that He is stronger than any storm

verse.text: You of little faith, why are you so afraid?

blocks.text: Storm quiz! Who is strong enough for your storms?

blocks.question: When the storm came, why didn't the wise man's house fall?
options: Because it was built on the rock
blocks.explain: Yes! The house on the rock stood. Build your life on Jesus, the Rock.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He built you on the Rock
Ask Him to make you firm and unshakeable

verse.text: For I am the Lord your God who takes hold of your right hand and says to you, Do not fear; I will help you.

blocks.text: What a picture for rest day: God holding your right hand. Walking through a storm never has to be alone — the strongest hand in the universe holds yours. Rest is safe tonight.

blocks.prompt: Draw your hand and God's hand holding yours in the middle of a storm.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for taking you by the hand
Ask Him to help you not fear

verse.text: The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.

blocks.text: Some storms leave us really hurting. God is not far away then — He is CLOSE to the brokenhearted. Write a prayer for the deep-root days: what you trust God for even when it is hard.

blocks.prompt: Write a prayer you can say on a stormy day — your deep-root prayer.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give God the things that feel stormy
Thank Him that He is close to the brokenhearted

intro.text: A garden's most wonderful day is the giving day — when the harvest goes out to the table and the friends. This final week of Spring is about the happiest secret of all: giving.

verse.text: God loves a cheerful giver.

blocks.text: God loves when you give — and He even loves HOW you give. A cheerful giver gives with a smile, not a grumble. The happy secret: giving grows more happiness than keeping.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one thing cheerfully today — a snack, a turn, a gift
Give with a real smile, not a grumble
Watch what giving does to your own heart

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make you a cheerful giver
Thank Him for giving us so much

verse.text: Do not forget to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.

blocks.text: The harvest is for sharing. God is pleased — happy — when we do good and share. A garden that keeps all its fruit to itself rots; a garden that shares keeps giving all season.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Share something you love, not just something extra
Do a good deed with no one watching
Say: 'my garden is for giving'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the harvest of your spring
Ask Him to make you generous

verse.text: A friend loves at all times.

blocks.text: The best garden has friends in it. 'A friend loves at all times' — on the fun days and the hard days. You and your family, your church, your club: souls growing in one garden.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be a 'at all times' friend to someone today
Thank a friend who has loved you on a hard day
Make one new friend seem welcome

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for your friends and family
Ask Him to make you a faithful friend

verse.text: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; his love endures forever.

blocks.text: People say thank you to God for everything this season grew. His love 'endures forever' — it never runs out, like a spring that never stops. Thanks is the garden's last and longest song.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: List the season's harvest and thank God for each
Say Psalm 107:1 at dinner
Tell someone why God is good to you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give thanks to the Lord — He is good
Thank Him for the love that endures forever

verse.text: Whoever sows generously will also reap generously.

blocks.text: The last quiz of Spring! Pick the giving answer.

blocks.question: Who does God love?
blocks.explain: Yes! 'God loves a cheerful giver.' Share with a smile, and God is pleased.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the joy of giving
Ask Him to make you sow generously all your life

verse.text: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; they will grow like a cedar of Lebanon.

blocks.text: Rest day before our last one. Palms and cedars grow slow and strong, and that is what a righteous life does — it flourishes over time. You have been a little plant all Spring; you are becoming a tree.

blocks.prompt: Draw or describe the tree you are becoming after thirteen weeks of Spring.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for how you have flourished
Ask Him to grow you like a strong tree

verse.text: Those who sow with tears will reap with songs of joy.

blocks.text: Today is the last day of Spring — the harvest celebration! From a tiniest seed on 1 September to songs of joy on 30 November. Celebrate everything God grew in you, share the harvest, and get ready: summer grows more.

blocks.prompt: Write a thank-you note to the Gardener — what did He grow in you this Spring?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Reap your season with songs of joy
Thank the Gardener for the whole of Spring
